newsitem.title: BULGARIA: BULGARIA COURT RULES BANK FOR AGRICREDIT INSOLVENT.
newsitem.headline: BULGARIA COURT RULES BANK FOR AGRICREDIT INSOLVENT.

text.p: The Sofia City Court declared the Bank for Agricultural Credit (BAC) insolvent at the request of the Bulgarian National Bank (BNB), a BNB official said on Monday.
"The court ruled in favour of the central bank insolvency claim against the Bank for Agricultural Credit," a BNB Legal Department official told Reuters.
The court decision dated July 18 can be appealed within seven days after being pubilshed in the State Gazette, the official added. The next issue of the State Gazette is due on Tuesday.
Under the ruling the BAC has been insolvent since December 6, 1996.
Tatiana Stefanova was appointed as an administrator to manage the bankruptcy.
In March 1996 the BNB acquired some 52 percent of the bank in a bid to protect depositors' savings and filed an insolvency suit against it in January.
The Bank Consolidation Company (BCC), which manages state equity in local commercial banks holds 25.1 percent of the BAC voting shares.

The BAC is the seventh Bulgarian commercial bank declared insolvent by courts so far out of a total of 17 local state and private banks against which the BNB has opened bankruptcy procedures since May 1996.
Those bankrupt included state-owned Mineralbank, the private Krystalbank, Private Agricultural and Investment bank, Trade and Savings Bank (TSB), Slavyani Bank and Agrobusinessbank.

So far the BNB has withdrawn its insolvency claims against two of the 17 banks after they were bought - Mollovbank, which later was re-named to Eurobank, and Yambol Bank. -- Roumiana Tikholova, Sofia Newsroom, 359-2-91188
